uutiset.t: How Volatility is Undermining the Carry Trade
uutiset.s: The carry trade, in which investors borrow in currencies like the yen, euro, and dollar, is becoming harder to navigate after delivering strong returns earlier in the year. Bloomberg's Garfield Reynolds discusses how market changes are impacting the strategy's appeal. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: IMF Urges RBA to Be Ready to Tighten Further If Prices Worsen
uutiset.s: Australia’s monetary authorities should stand ready to raise interest rates further if price pressures are more persistent, the International Monetary Fund said, while calling on the government to deliver on pledges to tighten fiscal policy.

uutiset.t: Brazil Assets Rally After Lula Names Banker as Finance Minister
uutiset.s: Brazilian assets gained after one of the country’s best-known bankers was named the new finance minister.

uutiset.t: Modi Critics Face Growing Constraints on Travel, Speech in India
uutiset.s: When activist Saurav Das tried to board a flight from New Delhi to London this week, Indian authorities stopped him from leaving the country. Days earlier, a Norwegian journalist critical of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government faced the opposite problem: she was prevented from entering.

uutiset.t: Singapore Wealth Firm Farro Plans Hong Kong Office With 20 Hires
uutiset.s: Singapore-based multi-family office Farro Capital is expanding to Hong Kong, with a plan to hire 20 staff and manage an additional $1 billion in the city within 18 months.

uutiset.t: Japan GPIF to Brief on Every Asset-Mix Review, Not Just Some
uutiset.s: Japan’s Government Pension Investment Fund is now reporting the results of every review of its strategic asset allocation to its board, rather than only sometimes when deemed necessary.

uutiset.t: Japan Tobacco Shares Climb on Potential Imperial Brands Takeover
uutiset.s: Japan Tobacco Inc. shares gained after news that the cigarette maker is exploring a potential takeover of Imperial Brands Plc with Altria Group Inc.

uutiset.t: US Plans for Tariffs Face Pushback
uutiset.s: Trading partners have responded to the latest US tariff plans with a mix of disappointment and protests, while some hold out the prospect for negotiations. Bloomberg's North Asia correspondent Minmin Low says China and the EU have made it clear that they will retaliate if necessary. (Source: Bloombe

uutiset.t: China Tech’s Earnings Offer Little Relief in Worst-Ever Year
uutiset.s: A gloomy earnings season for China tech is threatening to deepen the rout in the sector’s shares, as ballooning artificial intelligence spending and US chip curbs weigh on the outlook.

uutiset.t: Gold Steadies as Fed Rate Path and AI Stocks Frame Volatile Week
uutiset.s: Gold steadied, as traders weighed the prospect of Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes against a wider market recovery spurred by a rebound in US technology stocks.

uutiset.t: ‘Dollar Storm:’ Greenback on Track for Longest Winning Run Since 2024
uutiset.s: The dollar is poised for its longest monthly winning streak in two years as a rupture in the artificial intelligence trade and rising interest rates spur demand for safe-haven assets.

uutiset.t: Japan Bank Shares Risk Further Unwind as Funding Cost Bites
uutiset.s: Japanese banking shares face increasing risk of an unwind as higher interest rates provide less of a boost to profits amid intensifying competition across the sector.

uutiset.t: Lula Taps Bradesco Chair as Finance Chief to Soothe Markets
uutiset.s: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva tapped Bradesco Chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi as finance minister, turning to one of Brazil’s best-known bankers to restore investor confidence in the nation’s finances.

uutiset.t: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Nov. 27
uutiset.s: Oil was on track for the first weekly gain this month as attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers in the Middle East raised concerns escalating hostilities could disrupt exports.

uutiset.t: Bankers Pay Up for Hong Kong Apartments as Rents Hit New Highs
uutiset.s: Hong Kong’s booming rental real estate market is spurring gains in previously underappreciated neighborhoods, as bankers pay up for apartments in one of the world’s most expensive places to live.
